scope: Work-energy native candidate; extends, does not rewrite, the lot-0 review record in REFERENCES_V1.json.

references.title: FASTSim: A Model to Estimate Vehicle Efficiency, Cost and Performance
references.review_depth: Full PDF available; abstract and Powertrain Components/Vehicle/Fuel Converter/Motor/Battery sections on PDF pages1–3 read; not a complete source-code or validation-data replication.
references.adoption: Motivates reduced component energy flows, explicit losses/limits and separation of component model from calibration. No FASTSim coefficients, efficiency curve or source code copied. Newtonian work-energy equations and discretization derived in Pitgun.
references.limitation: Drive-cycle fuel-economy validation of FASTSim is not validation of racing tires or Pitgun lap times.

references.title: ME420 Lecture7: Conduction — 1D Fins and Lumped Capacitance
references.review_depth: Scanned primary course PDF; rendered PDF pages7–9 (handwritten60–62) visually reviewed. Pages7–8 contain aggregate thermal balance, exponential cooling, isothermal assumption and small Biot criterion.
references.adoption: C dT/dt = Q - H(T-Tamb), constant-input exact step independently derived; Q is the additional held heat source. Numerical expm1/adiabatic treatment implemented and tested locally.
references.limitation: The course states a uniform-temperature/small-Biot assumption. An aggregate engine temperature is a reduced proxy; no validation of Pitgun engine heat capacity, conductance, heat fraction or multi-node engine temperature is supplied.

publication_rule: Cite primary sections actually read; distinguish adopted balance law, numerical derivation, empirical coefficients and external accuracy validation.
